name: @archstone/cli
stderr:
usage: archstone <apply|serve|verify|build|diff|doctor|init|adopt|audit>

       archstone <apply|serve|verify|build> <manifest-dir> [--json] [--out path]
       archstone apply <manifest-dir> --exposure [--json]
         per capability: what a model receives, what it is shown, and what the backend was
         observed to return that it never sees — names and types only (--json: that report alone)
       archstone verify <manifest-dir> [--json] [--sandbox] [--identity-map <file>]
         --sandbox: also replay `write`/`irreversible` fixtures — they are skipped by default,
         because a replay is a real invocation. Only for a backend you know is a sandbox tenant.
       archstone serve [--http] <manifest-dir> [--port <n>] [--token <value>] [--identity-map <file>] [--sql-guc-prefix <prefix>]
         bearer token (--http only): --token <value>, or the ARCHSTONE_HTTP_TOKEN env var (required — never serves open)
         --identity-map <file> / ARCHSTONE_IDENTITY_MAP: a JSON file mapping a resolved caller
         principal to sql session identity claims (ADR-0012) — required for any sql-bound capability
         to be invocable at all; absent means every sql invocation refuses (fail-closed)
         --sql-guc-prefix <prefix> / ARCHSTONE_SQL_GUC_PREFIX: session GUC name prefix (default "app.")
       archstone diff <before> <after> [--json] [--all]
         what changed for an agent between two declarations; each side is a built .json
         artifact or a manifest dir. Exits 1 iff a change is breaking. --all lists compatible ones
       archstone doctor <manifest-dir> [--json]  — pre-production checks, offline
       archstone init <spec-file> --out <dir>   — start here if you have no manifest yet
       archstone adopt <manifest-dir>
         declare a field the backend started returning; asks before writing, needs a person

       archstone audit <file...> [--since <date>] [--format summary|jsonl|csv]
         read your own Execution audit records; nothing is uploaded (audit --help for filters)

       archstone --version | --help

usage: archstone init <spec-file> --out <dir> [options]

  Read an API description, ask you the questions no tool can answer, and write a CDL
  manifest the real compiler has already compiled. No LLM is involved, on any path.

  --out <dir>            where the manifest goes (required)
  --domain <name>        the domain half of every capability id (e.g. 'framing')
  --company <id>         company id, lowercase kebab (e.g. 'acme')
  --decisions <file>     a Decision Record JSON file, instead of the interactive gate.
                         Each entry's `operation` is the CANDIDATE KEY, which is
                         `<METHOD> <path>` with the path INCLUDING the server base path
                         from `servers[0].url` — so a document whose `paths:` reads
                         `/catalog/frames` under a server of `https://api.x.test/api/v1`
                         has the key `GET /api/v1/catalog/frames`. Run without --decisions
                         once to see the real keys, or read them off a failed run's report.
                         Not combinable with --company or --domain, which it answers.
  --report <file>        also write the report here (default: <out>/INIT-REPORT.md)
  --probe                OPT-IN, READ-ONLY. Record a golden fixture by making ONE live
                         request per capability you consent to. Never issued for a
                         capability whose confirmed effect is not `read`; a non-GET/HEAD
                         method needs a second, separate confirmation, and is refused
                         outright when there is no terminal. Off by default.
  --non-interactive      no prompts. Requires --decisions: `init` never defaults an
                         `effect`, so with no human and no record there is nothing to do.
  --force                write into a non-empty directory
